## What the contribution is (and is not)
The machinery is classical: item selection by A-/D-optimal design for a latent trait vector (multidimensional computerized adaptive testing, Mulder & van der Linden 2009), cold-start active learning for matrix factorisation (Rashid 2002, Golbandi 2011, Houlsby 2014), probabilistic PCA, greedy subset selection with submodularity-ratio guarantees. **I do not claim a new selection method.** The contribution is: (i) the empirical answer on real leaderboard matrices under the protocol that matches the use (whole new models held out, by group; selection fit on others only); (ii) a sufficiency rule k*(ε) tied to the spectrum of the matrix, with its misfit term made explicit; (iii) the **scope map**: where the answer holds and where it never reaches the floor (extrapolation to new families/strongest models, sparse coverage, small M, saturated scores, task granularity), including a misspecification ladder on synthetic data on which real matrices are placed.

## Model and selection
- y_{mj} = μ_j + v_jᵀ z_m + ε_{mj}, ε~N(0,σ_j²) on standardised scores, fitted by EM on observed cells (probabilistic PCA/FA with missing data); transform/link as a sensitivity variant.
- New model: posterior of z given the run set S. Selection objective with a **fixed target**: F(S) = tr(V Σ_post(S) Vᵀ) over all benchmarks (or a weighted version / the unrun-only variant; compared empirically). Greedy; the Das–Kempe / Bian et al. guarantee is reported but may be vacuous at low noise, so greedy is checked against exhaustive search (small N) and swap/local search. Posterior covariance is independent of y, so selection is an offline subset problem per run-set restriction. Cost-aware variant (gain per cost, equal-cost random comparator) only if a real cost source exists (MTEB `evaluation_time`, to be confirmed), else dropped or a stated proxy.

## Theory (stated with assumptions; each checked)
- **T1 (risk decomposition).** Under the model with *known* parameters: E err_j(S) = σ_j² + v_jᵀ(I + V_SᵀΣ_S⁻¹V_S)⁻¹v_j. With parameters estimated from M models there is an additional estimation term, predicted to scale ~1/M. Empirical risk(k) = residual floor + design term(k) + misfit(k); the misfit term is reported on real data.
- **T2 (shape of the curve).** Two regimes, stated before results: with separated factors (eigenvalues ≫ σ²) a knee near effective rank r; with decaying spectrum a gradual closure and ~1/k decay whose constant depends on the incoherence of the loadings. Effective rank is defined *before* looking at results (parallel analysis, eigenvalues above the noise edge, CV-selected rank; sensitivity to imputation reported). k*(ε) = smallest k whose predicted design term ≤ ε, in raw score points as well as standardised units.
- **T3 (adaptive = batch)** — a one-paragraph proposition (known V, σ², Gaussian, squared loss, fixed run set; textbook), verified as a unit test under the same posterior. The empirical question is what adaptivity gains where assumptions fail (tree/kNN interviews test misspecification, not T3).
- **T4 (random-k near-optimal beyond r + margin)** — a conjecture supported by simulation; appendix.
"Residual floor" is not measurement noise: it is variance unexplained by rank-r structure (noise + misfit + family effects). Leaderboard cells are single measurements.

## Hypotheses (pre-registered branches)
H1 matrices are close to low-rank (rank by the stated estimator). H2 designed selection beats random-k with the same inference for k below ~r and the gap closes afterwards. H3 measured curve follows T1/T2 on synthetic data (with estimation term) and on real data up to the reported misfit. H4 adaptivity gains only under misspecification. H5 conclusions weaken, quantifiably, under extrapolation, sparsity, small M, saturation, granularity.

shown.message:
The interim results change the idea, and I've reworded the contribution in Brief rev. 7 (wiki). I closed `story-repo`'s request #8 after replying. I didn't run anything myself; the numbers below are from `experiment-repo`'s interim files.

**What the interim results say** (MTEB, 238 models × 328 tasks, group hold-out):
- **Needed k:** about 20 of the 328 tasks (6%) get within roughly 1 point RMSE of using all the other tasks. The interval for that k is [12, 32].
- **Design versus random-k:** designed selection beats random-k clearly for k ≤ 5 (about 1.7–1.8 points at k ≤ 3, 1.2 at k=5). The gain is about 0.5 points at k = 8–20 and the two are within noise by k ≈ 32. The negative branch ("random-k suffices beyond small k") is not taken as stated.
- **Resolution:** the all-others floor is about 5.7 points, far above the median gap between adjacent models (about 0.17). No k resolves neighbouring models; what k buys is coarse placement.
- **Limits:** these runs score on each model's remaining observed cells, not yet on the common target set. Headline numbers must come from the rerun.

**Decisions in rev. 7:**
- **Contribution:** it is now the empirical needed-k curve plus an error decomposition that attributes where the error sits. The spectrum-based rule for k did not carry on real data: it predicted 3 where 20 was measured. I report that failure as a result. The design term is small and correctly sized, and the misfit term (11.0 of 44.8 MSE at k=20) is what the rule misses.
- **Rank:** I dropped the "rank r" claim, because the rank estimators disagree (5 to 56) and one component carries 63% of the variance.
- **Main message:** designed selection matters only for very small k. After that the error is the floor plus model misfit, so better inference, not better selection, is what would help.
- **Margin:** my pre-set margin δ was set by the adjacent-model gap (about 0.1 points), below anything attainable at any k. That was my mistake for this matrix. Both scales are reported, and nothing is relabelled after the fact.
- **Exploratory rule:** a data-driven k rule extrapolated from the training-side reveal curve, labelled post-hoc because I thought of it after seeing the results.

I opened `experiment-repo` issue #5 with three asks:
- Rerun on the common target set and record the amendment as made after the interim results. The Brief's rev. 4 and 5 timestamps show the protocol preceded any result.
- Show which rung of the synthetic misspecification ladder reproduces the misfit.
- Test the exploratory rule.

My commitment issue #2 stays open.
